entities.summary: Pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty (r. c. 1479–1425 BCE), often called the "Napoleon of Egypt" for his military genius. After emerging from the co-regency with his stepmother Hatshepsut, Thutmose III conducted at least 17 military campaigns, expanding Egypt to its greatest territorial extent from the Fourth Cataract in Nubia to the Euphrates in Syria. His Annals, inscribed on the walls of the Temple of Karnak, provide the most detailed military records from the ancient world, including the Battle of Megiddo (c. 1457 BCE) — the earliest battle recorded in sufficient detail to be analyzed strategically.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Thutmose III's military campaigns expanded Egypt to its greatest territorial extent, with at least 17 campaigns covering a vast area from Nubia to Syria. His detailed records of the Battle of Megiddo provide valuable insights into ancient warfare.
